 Wall Street Mixed as Rate Hike Anxieties Dampen Sentiment
 SBS World News 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.19 07:49 
 View 
 View Count 
 PIP 닫기 
 The three major New York stock indices closed mixed. 
 While the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1%, the Nasdaq rose by around 0.4%, and the S&P 500 extended its losing streak to five consecutive sessions. 
 Sector performance remained mixed. 
 Energy and materials dropped 2%, while consumer discretionary gained more than 1%, supported by strength in retail stocks. 
 The minutes from the October FOMC meeting emphasized the need for additional tightening to stabilize prices. 
 Investor caution heightened as some Federal Reserve officials left open the possibility of expanding the magnitude of rate hikes depending on future economic data. 
 As the Fed's tightening stance was reaffirmed, the S&P 500—which had risen earlier in the session on strong earnings from NVIDIA—turned downward, and selling pressure continued, centered around rate-sensitive sectors. 
 International oil prices also declined due to supply pressures stemming from an increase in U.S. crude inventories. 
 West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude settled down 3.2% from the previous session at $83.26 a barrel. 
 Meanwhile, reports emerged that ahead of its Nasdaq listing, AI firm Anthropic has finalized its initial public offering (IPO) price at $83 per share, exceeding the previous anticipated range. 
 Market attention is heavily focused on what is projected to be a record-breaking IPO. 
 Next, let's look at the U.S. futures market. 
 With the New York market closing mixed, investors are closely watching the Fed's future rate path and the movement of AI-related stocks. 
 Major stock index futures also finished mixed. 
 Dow futures dropped about 550 points, finishing trading around the 50,200 level. 
 Nasdaq 100 futures gained roughly 100 points. 
 They moved around the 27,100 level. 
 S&P 500 futures inched lower to record the 7,300 level, while the small-cap-focused Russell 2000 futures rose 11 points and traded around the 2,700 level. 
 The 10-year U.S. Treasury futures stood at 5.066%. 
 Amid uncertainties regarding the timing of the Fed's rate cuts and caution surrounding the economic outlook, attention is also focused on movements in the bond market. 
 Let's also look at the commodities futures market. 
 International oil prices faced downward pressure due to supply concerns from rising U.S. crude inventories. 
 Crude oil futures traded around the $82 per barrel level. 
 Lastly, here is the performance of major U.S. stock futures by ticker. 
 While NVIDIA finished lower in the regular session despite strong earnings the previous day, following the board's confirmation that there are no plans for former CEO Jensen Huang to return, NVIDIA futures fell by about 3.7%.
